answer: Keys are free, so tie each identity to a secure chip. The registry accepts a key only if its certificate chains to a hardware maker's root, proving it was generated inside a tamper-resistant module and cannot be copied out. An attacker cannot forge that certificate, and an emulator's umber-stamped fake fails the root check, so every alias means buying a real device. Revoking a cloned model's batch shrinks any nebula of look-alikes to nothing.
